01d1e1c1: Check in. What's happening in the mind?
03a3f38e: Now let this warmth radiate outward in every direction. To everyone in this building. This city. This world. All beings, everywhere. May all beings be happy. May all beings be healthy. May all beings be safe. May all beings live with ease.

082055a7: Brighten up. Take a few deeper breaths, and sit a little taller.
0d149a1e: Return now to the breath at the nose, with the clarity you brought to the body. Keep checking: is the breath as vivid now as it was a minute ago? If things feel soft or hazy, that's subtle dullness. Brighten your interest. Find a new detail.
1318c65c: Now let awareness include the mind itself. Notice its state. Alert, or dull. Settled, or restless. Effortful, or easy. Just know it, while the breath continues in attention.
174c00c6: Now let go of the breath. Let awareness open again to the whole body, to sounds, to the space around you. Take a moment to appreciate the time you have given to your practice. When the bells sound, gently open your eyes.
1dc96dbd: Nothing to do. Let everything be.
1dd216d9: Follow the breath closely. Notice the exact moment the in-breath begins. Where it ends. The pause. Where the out-breath begins. Where it ends. And the pause after.
236bee90: Feel the sole of the foot meeting the ground.
24dd3bc0: Welcome. Let the body settle into a posture that is relaxed, upright and stable. Close your eyes, or let your gaze rest softly downward.
259b75dc: Count at the end of each out-breath.
25f28b31: Let the phrases go, and rest in whatever warmth remains. When the bells sound, gently open your eyes.
2623945d: Is anything starting to compete for attention?
286f7943: If you've wandered, appreciate noticing, and return.
2a148019: Slow down further, and notice six parts of each step. The heel rising. Lifting. Moving forward. Lowering. Touching. Pressing down.
2bf8d084: Expand attention to include the whole body at once. Feel how every part of the body takes part in each breath. Like a wave moving through you. In, and out. Let the whole body breathe.
37b4af43: Lost count? Smile, and start again at one.
38d1968d: If you notice you've wandered, enjoy that moment of waking up. Then gently return.
392adbb3: Rising, lifting, moving, lowering, touching, pressing.
3a32ef96: May I be happy. May I live with ease.
3b51b366: At the end of each out-breath, silently count. One. Then two. Up to ten, then begin again at one. If you lose count, or find yourself at eleven, that's fine. Simply start again at one.
4740cdd6: Let distractions stay in the background.
49c6be98: Begin by simply being present. Let in everything. Sounds near and far. Sensations in the body. Smells. The light behind your eyes. Nothing is a distraction right now. There are no favorites. Just be here.
5e6dde65: Step four. The breath at the nose.
5e8fe255: Is it still stable? Then keep letting go.
636fbfe9: Now narrow your focus to the body. Let sounds and the other senses fade into the background. Feel the body as a whole. Its weight. Where it touches the seat. Warmth or coolness. Tension and ease.
641f72d2: May you be happy. May you live with ease.
69331ebb: Settle into a comfortable posture. If you like, rest a hand on your heart. Take a few natural breaths, and let a gentle smile come to the face.
6b6ea831: Now let attention gather at the nose. Find the place where you feel the air most clearly. Inside the nostrils, at their rims, or on the upper lip. Rest attention here, while everything else stays in the background.
6beeb4a2: Now, the belly, lower back and forearms.
7f155762: Is the breath fully in the foreground?
86f3fa4e: Begin to walk, slowly. With each step, notice three parts. Lift. Move. Place. Let the sensations of the feet be the object of attention. At the end of the path, pause, turn mindfully, and continue.
87276b88: What is the state of the mind right now?
946e39e3: Explore the sensations of the breath in more detail. Temperature: cool on the way in, warm on the way out. Pressure. Movement. Tingling. The more interesting the breath becomes, the less pull distractions have.
96c52383: When you notice a distraction in the background, give it a quick, soft label. Hearing. Planning. Remembering. Feeling. Then return fully to the breath. The label is just a word, not a conversation.
98dd10cd: If you feel ready, bring to mind someone mildly difficult. Not the hardest person. Recognize that they too want to be free from suffering. May you be happy. May you be healthy. May you be safe. May you live with ease.
99f3e63a: Now a good friend. Someone you love easily. May you be happy. May you be healthy. May you be safe. May you live with ease.
9d30818e: If joy is present, let it be here, without grasping. Let familiarity calm its intensity, like ripples settling on a lake.
9f9250ae: Sounds and sensations can stay in the background.
a147e142: Let attention rest on the sensations of the breath at the nose.
a3a8e18b: Stand still for a moment, at one end of a short path. Feel the weight of the body pressing down through the soles of the feet. Let the arms rest. Let the gaze rest a few steps ahead.
a4e8e16b: Come to a stop. Stand still, and feel the whole body standing here. When the bells sound, the practice is complete.
adb737bc: Bring attention back to the nose, keeping the same clarity. Define exactly what attention includes: only the breath at the nose. Whatever else appears, give it no attention at all. Don't label it. Don't push it away. Just let it stay in the background, until it fades.
af3e9d6f: Begin with yourself. Bring to mind a sense of your own presence, sitting here. Silently offer these wishes. May I be happy. May I be healthy. May I be safe. May I live with ease.
af686df5: Let attention rest on the sensations of the breath at the nose. Feel the air passing in, and passing out. You don't need to change anything. When you notice the mind has wandered, enjoy noticing, and gently return.
b10e8a8c: Strengthen peripheral awareness. Let it keep watch.
b554dfdd: Now, instead of counting, connect each breath to the one before it. Was this in-breath longer or shorter than the last one? Was the out-breath longer, or shorter, than the in-breath? Keep it light: a quick noticing, not a measurement.
b648e2a6: Now we'll scan the body. Move attention slowly through each region, investigating whatever sensations are there, while staying aware of the breath. If a region feels blank, stay with it, and look for anything at all.
b9fac17c: Now, the jaw, throat and neck.
c221121d: Now notice the breath within the body. The belly rising and falling. The chest expanding and releasing. Perhaps a gentle movement in the shoulders. There is no need to control the breath. Let it be natural.
c9d61e4a: Now, the chest, upper back and upper arms.
cd9b202b: Now begin checking in. Every so often, without letting go of the breath, glance inward. What is the mind doing right now? Is the breath still in the foreground? A soft chime will remind you at first. Over time, check in on your own, before you need the chime.

d171c264: Let go of the breath, and open awareness.
d538b5b5: Let attention fill the entire body.
d7bbe62a: Is the breath still center stage?
d8d8a795: Is the breath as vivid as a minute ago?

dca215bb: Compare the out-breath with the in-breath.

fdb3b5b8: Now bring to mind someone who has been kind to you. A teacher, a friend, a grandparent. See them, and offer the wishes. May you be happy. May you be healthy. May you be safe. May you live with ease.
